cards.q: How many people died from tuberculosis in 2025?
How many of the 2025 tuberculosis deaths were among people with HIV?
Where does TB rank among all causes of death globally?
What is the world's leading cause of death from a single infectious agent?
How many people were estimated to have fallen ill with TB worldwide in 2025?
What was the estimated breakdown of people who fell ill with TB in 2025?
cards.a: 5.7 million men, 3.7 million women and 1.2 million children.

cards.q: What proportion of people with drug-resistant TB accessed treatment in 2025?
How many lives have global efforts to combat TB saved since the year 2000?
What proportion of the global population is estimated to have been infected with TB bacteria?
What percentage of people infected with TB eventually develop TB disease?
What type of pathogen causes tuberculosis?
What does MDR-TB stand for?
What does BCG stand for in TB prevention?
According to WHO, how do people with TB infection generally feel and how contagious are they?
cards.a: They don't feel sick and are not contagious.

cards.q: How does TB spread through the air?
cards.a: When people with TB cough, sneeze or spit.

cards.q: When does TB disease occur, as opposed to TB infection?
cards.a: When bacteria multiply in the body and affect different organs.

cards.q: Why is it easy to spread TB to others without knowing it?
cards.a: TB symptoms may be mild for many months.

cards.q: How is TB disease usually treated?
What can happen to TB disease without treatment?
What does the BCG vaccine protect children from?
cards.a: Serious forms of TB; it also prevents deaths from TB.

cards.q: Which age groups are at higher risk of developing TB disease if infected?
What determines which symptoms a person with TB disease develops?
cards.a: Which part of the body is affected.

cards.q: Besides the lungs, which organs can TB affect?
Which conditions increase a person's risk for TB disease?
cards.a: Diabetes, a weakened immune system (for example from HIV), undernutrition, tobacco use, and harmful use of alcohol.

cards.q: Is tuberculosis preventable and curable?
cards.a: Yes — TB is preventable and curable.

cards.q: How does WHO characterise multidrug-resistant TB as a threat?
cards.a: As a public health crisis and a health security threat.
